units.title: Polynomials
units.intro: Terms of form a_n x^n+…+a0. Degree = highest power. Add like terms. Multiply: distribute every term. Special: (a+b)²=a²+2ab+b², (a−b)²=a²−2ab+b², (a+b)(a−b)=a²−b².

cards.title: 8.1 What is a polynomial?
body: A **polynomial** in $x$ is a sum of terms $a x^n$ where each $a$ is a real number and each exponent $n$ is a **whole number** (0, 1, 2, …): $$a_n x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1} + \dots + a_1 x + a_0, \quad a_n \ne 0$$
Examples from a cube of side $x$: perimeter of the base $4x$ (linear), base area $x^2$ (quadratic), volume $x^3$ (cubic).
- **Degree** = the highest power ($n$). **Leading coefficient** = $a_n$. **Constant term** = $a_0$.
- **Standard form**: powers in decreasing order: $-11x^7 - 2x^6 + 0.5x^3 - 12x + 9$.
- **Like terms** have the same variables with the same powers ($3x^2$ and $-5x^2$); $3x^2$ and $3x^4$ are unlike.
- By number of terms: **monomial** (1), **binomial** (2), **trinomial** (3).
The zero polynomial 0 has **no degree**.

steps.text: A polynomial cannot contain negative exponents, fractional exponents, or variables in denominators.
The expression $$3x^{-2} + 4$$ contains a variable raised to a negative exponent ($$-2$$), which violates the polynomial rules.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Classify the polynomial expression $$5x - 9$$ by its number of terms.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Count the number of unlike terms**
The expression $$5x - 9$$ consists of exactly two unlike terms: $$5x$$ and $$-9$$.

**Step 2: Classify based on count**
A polynomial with exactly two unlike terms is a **binomial**.

**Step 3: Final Result**
It is a **binomial**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If $$A(x) = x^2 - 5x - 7$$ and $$B(x) = 7x^2 - 4x + 10$$, find their sum $$A(x) + B(x)$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Group like terms horizontally**
$$A(x) + B(x) = (x^2 + 7x^2) + (-5x - 4x) + (-7 + 10)$$

**Step 2: Combine the coefficients**
$$A(x) + B(x) = 8x^2 - 9x + 3$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The sum is **$$8x^2 - 9x + 3$$**.

**Step 3: Final Result**

cards.title: 8.2.1 Adding polynomials
body: You can only add **like terms** (8 goats + 4 goats = 12 goats, but 8 goats + 4 dogs stays as it is): add their **coefficients**, keep the power.
**Horizontal:** group like terms: $(x^2 - 5x - 7) + (7x^2 - 4x + 10) = 8x^2 - 9x + 3$.
**Vertical:** write in standard form, line up equal powers (use $0x^k$ for gaps) and add the columns.
Common mistake (Activity 8.3): $3x^3 + 4x^2$ is **not** $7x^5$ — unlike terms cannot be combined, and powers are never added when you add.

cards.title: 8.2.2 Subtracting polynomials
body: Subtracting = adding the **opposite**: change the sign of **every** term of the polynomial being subtracted, then add.
"Subtract $A$ from $B$" means $B - A$ (the order is reversed in words!).
The usual error is changing only the first sign: $(x^2 - 4x + 4) - (x^2 + 5x - 1) \ne x^2 - 4x + 4 - x^2 + 5x - 1$.

steps.text: Change every sign of the second: $7m^3 - 4m + 11 + 3m^2 - 5m - 9$.

cards.title: 8.2.3 Multiplying polynomials
body: **Monomial × monomial:** multiply coefficients, **add** exponents of the same variable: $(-2x^3)(4x^2) = -8x^5$; $(2ab^2)(3a^2b) = 6a^3b^3$.
**Monomial × polynomial:** distribute: $-7x(-3 + 2x) = 21x - 14x^2$.
**Polynomial × polynomial:** multiply **every** term of the first by **every** term of the second, then collect like terms: $(x - 3)(5x - 1) = 5x^2 - x - 15x + 3 = 5x^2 - 16x + 3$.
Check the count: a binomial × trinomial gives $2 \times 3 = 6$ products before collecting. The degree of a product = sum of the degrees.

cards.title: Special products
body: - **Sum × difference:** $(a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2$. The middle terms cancel: $(5x + 3)(5x - 3) = 25x^2 - 9$.
- **Square of a difference:** $(a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2$: $(2x - 3y)^2 = 4x^2 - 12xy + 9y^2$.
**Biggest mistake:** $(a + b)^2 \ne a^2 + b^2$ — you forget $2ab$. Check: $(2 + 3)^2 = 25$ but $4 + 9 = 13$.

cards.title: Why (a + b)² has a middle term

steps.text: Draw a square of side $a + b$. Its area is $(a + b)^2$.
Cut it: one $a \times a$ square, one $b \times b$ square and **two** $a \times b$ rectangles.
Total: $a^2 + 2ab + b^2$. The two rectangles are the $2ab$ that people forget.

cards.title: 8.2.4 Dividing polynomials
body: **By a monomial:** split the fraction and divide each term (subtract exponents): $\frac{6x^3 - 15x^2 + 12x}{3x} = 2x^2 - 5x + 4$ ($x \ne 0$).
**By factorising:** if the dividend factorises with the divisor as a factor, cancel it: $(x^2 + 7x + 10) \div (x + 5) = \frac{(x + 5)(x + 2)}{x + 5} = x + 2$.

**Long division** (always works): 1. Write both in standard form and insert $0x^k$ for missing powers. 2. Divide the first term by the first term. 3. Multiply back and **subtract**. 4. Bring down and repeat. 5. Stop when the remainder's degree is **less** than the divisor's.

Check: **dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder**. (The textbook says division "makes sense only when the degree of the dividend is equal to or less than" the divisor's — it is the other way round: the dividend's degree must be **at least** the divisor's.)

steps.text: $3x^2 \div x = 3x$: the first term of the quotient.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the degree of the polynomial expression $$4x^3 - 7x - 5$$?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Understand the definition of degree**
The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable present in the expression.

**Step 2: Analyze the given polynomial**
In $$4x^3 - 7x - 5$$, the exponents of $$x$$ are 3 (in $$4x^3$$) and 1 (in $$-7x$$). The highest exponent is 3.

**Step 3: Final Result**
The degree of the polynomial is **$$3$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Simplify the product of the monomials: $$(-2x^3)(4x^2)$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Multiply the coefficients**
$$-2 \times 4 = -8$$

**Step 2: Apply the product law to exponents**
$$x^3 \times x^2 = x^{3+2} = x^5$$

**Step 3: Combine results**
$$(-2x^3)(4x^2) = -8x^5$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The simplified product is **$$-8x^5$$**.

cards.title: The four operations on polynomials
body: **Add/subtract:** combine like terms (same variable, same power). (3x² − 2x + 5) − (x² + 4x − 1) = 3x² − 2x + 5 − x² − 4x + 1 = 2x² − 6x + 6. Change every sign in the bracket after a minus.

**Multiply:** multiply every term of the first polynomial by every term of the second, then collect like terms: (x + 3)(2x − 1) = 2x² − x + 6x − 3 = 2x² + 5x − 3. Special products: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b², (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
**Divide:** long division as with numbers — divide the leading terms, multiply back, subtract, bring down. Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder.

steps.text: Step 1: x² ÷ x = x. Multiply x(x + 2) = x² + 2x and subtract: (x² + 5x) − (x² + 2x) = 3x. Bring down +7: 3x + 7.
Step 3: quotient x + 3, remainder 1. Check: (x + 2)(x + 3) + 1 = x² + 5x + 6 + 1 ✔.

cards.title: 8.3 Graphs of polynomial functions
body: A **polynomial function** is $y = a_n x^n + \dots + a_1 x + a_0$. Degree 1 → straight line; degree 2 → parabola; degree 3 → an S-shaped **cubic**.
**Drawing $y = x^3$:** make a table ($x = -2, -1.5, \dots, 2$ gives $y = -8, -3.4, -1, -0.13, 0, 0.13, 1, 3.4, 8$), plot and join with a smooth curve.
Facts about $y = x^3$: domain and range are all real numbers; it always rises; it passes through $(0, 0)$ only, but looks flat near 0 because small numbers cubed are tiny ($0.5^3 = 0.125$).
**$y = ax^3 + b$:** $b$ moves the graph up or down (y-intercept $b$); $a > 0$ rises left to right, $a < 0$ falls.

cards.title: End behaviour and the leading term
body: For large $|x|$ the leading term $a_n x^n$ dominates, so it decides where the two ends of the graph go:
- $a_n > 0$, $n$ even: both ends **up** (has a lowest point), e.g. $y = x^2 - 4$.
- $a_n > 0$, $n$ odd: left **down**, right **up**, e.g. $y = \frac{1}{2}x^3 + 2$.
- $a_n < 0$, $n$ even: both ends **down** (has a highest point), e.g. $y = -x^2 + 4$.
- $a_n < 0$, $n$ odd: left **up**, right **down**, e.g. $y = -\frac{1}{2}x^3$.
Reading a graph backwards: ends the same way → even degree; ends opposite → odd degree. Right end up → $a_n > 0$.

cards.title: Reading a cubic graph (Activity 8.16 Q3)
body: x-intercepts $-2$, 1, 3 (check: $f(1) = 1 - 2 - 5 + 6 = 0$). y-intercept 6 (the constant term). Two turning points near $x \approx -0.8$ and $x \approx 2.1$. The right end rises, the left end falls → odd degree, positive leading coefficient. Domain and range: all real numbers.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Expand the expression using special products: $$(5x + 3)(5x - 3)$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the special product pattern**
The expression matches the difference of squares formula: $$(a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2$$

**Step 2: Substitute $$a = 5x$$ and $$b = 3$$**
$$(5x + 3)(5x - 3) = (5x)^2 - 3^2$$

**Step 3: Simplify**
$$(5x)^2 - 3^2 = 25x^2 - 9$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The expanded expression is **$$25x^2 - 9$$**.

$$(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$$

**Step 2: Substitute $$b = 2$$**
$$(a + 2)^2 = a^2 + 2(a)(2) + 2^2$$

**Step 3: Simplify**
$$a^2 + 4a + 4$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The expanded trinomial is **$$a^2 + 4a + 4$$**.

cards.title: Step by step: sketching a polynomial graph
body: Step 1 — **end behaviour** from the leading term: even degree with positive leading coefficient → both ends up; odd degree with positive leading coefficient → left end down, right end up (reverse both if the leading coefficient is negative).
Step 2 — **y-intercept:** the constant term.
Step 3 — **zeros:** factor and solve f(x) = 0; mark them on the x-axis.
Step 4 — a few **test values** between the zeros to see whether the graph is above or below the axis.

**Example f(x) = x(x − 2)(x + 1) = x³ − x² − 2x:** odd degree, positive leading coefficient; y-intercept 0; zeros −1, 0, 2; f(−0.5) = 0.625 > 0 and f(1) = −2 < 0. The graph comes up from the bottom left, crosses at −1, turns, crosses at 0, dips, and crosses at 2 going up.

cards.title: Practice
cards.q: Which describes the ends of the graph of f(x) = −2x⁴ + x?
cards.why: The leading term −2x⁴ has even degree (both ends the same way) and a negative coefficient (down). So both ends go down.

questions.q: Divided by $5x^2 + 3x - 2$, a polynomial gives quotient $-3x + 1$ and remainder 10. Find it.
questions.tip: Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder.
questions.label: 8.2 Practice — operations

questions.q: For $y = x^3$: give the domain, range and intercepts. Does the graph go up or down for $x > 0$?
why: Step 2: every real number is a cube.
questions.tip: A cubic covers all $y$ values.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.q: How is $y = x^3 + 1$ related to $y = x^3$? Give its intercepts.
questions.tip: $+b$ moves up by $b$.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.tip: Only the leading term matters.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.q: Can a third-degree polynomial have no x-intercept? Give an example of one with three.
why: Step 1: its ends go opposite ways, so it must cross the x-axis.
questions.tip: Build from factors.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.q: The graph of $y = (x - 2)^2(x + 3)$ has x-intercepts at $-2$ and 3.
why: Step 1: set each factor to zero: $x = 2$, $x = -3$.
questions.tip: Factor $(x - k)$ ↔ intercept $+k$.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.tip: y-intercept = constant term, with its sign.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.q: A cubic and a quadratic: what is the degree of their sum, and of their product?
why: Step 1: the $x^3$ term cannot cancel, so the sum has degree 3.
questions.tip: Sum → highest; product → add degrees.

similar.q: Two cubics $x^3 + x$ and $-x^3 + 2$: degree of the sum?

questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.q: From the graph of $y = x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x + 6$, list the x-intercepts and the y-intercept, and verify one intercept.
questions.tip: Always check an intercept by substitution.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs

questions.q: Which could be the equation of a graph whose left end goes up, right end goes down and y-intercept is 3: $y = -2x^3 + 3$, $y = -2x^2 + 3$, $y = x^3 + 3$?
why: Step 2: right end down → negative leading coefficient.
questions.tip: Ends first, then intercepts.
questions.label: 8.3 Practice — graphs
